p.PROJECT-FOLLOWS-CODKIT-STANDARDS: This repository is a patch set maintained by codkit, and it follows the **codkit standards**, edition 0.2.0: the standard of minimal intervention in the fork — the delta as a parallel system in upstream's own style, every feature one folder behind a flag: @spec://org.vibevm.codkit/standards/flows/standards/minimal-intervention#root — and the catalogue of upstream seams it picks from: @spec://org.vibevm.codkit/standards/flows/standards/seam-catalogue#root.

p.HOW-A-STANDARD-BINDS: How a standard binds the project, how a deviation is recorded, who wins on conflict, and where the three licence scopes end: @spec://org.vibevm.codkit/standards/flows/standards/STANDARDS-PROTOCOL#root.

facts.LAW-PARALLEL-SYSTEM-FIRST: The delta is a parallel system in upstream's own style, not a pile of patches: for every intervention the first question is how upstream itself would build it — a service through DI, a workbench contribution, a registry, an extension point, `product.json`, a built-in extension — and that answer is the shape of own code; the seam comes second, the patch last.
facts.LAW-PATCH-IS-A-GRAFT: A patch is a graft: an import or one call that delegates into own code, three lines at most between the markers; logic never lives in a patch.
facts.LAW-FEATURE-HAS-A-FLAG: A new feature is one own folder behind a flag — a user setting, a policy-backed setting or a build value — and it toggles live where it can; a feature that cannot freezes at startup and asks for a restart.
facts.LAW-HIGHEST-LAYER-WINS: The layer chosen is the highest applicable one — the ladder and the decision tree come from the installed codkit (PROP-005 §1 `LAYER-CHOICE-RULE`, `docs/codkit/protocol/human/03-interventions.md`); the standard never restates them.
facts.LAW-NECESSITY-WINS: A feature the product requires is implemented even where only an invasive layer can express it; minimality then means the least invasive form of that intervention, never its omission — and an existing intervention that can be made less invasive is.
facts.LAW-CHOICE-IS-PRESENTED: The choice of layer is presented: the `reason` of every artifact below own names the rejected upper leaf and why; an intervention with no home in the product's specs gets one before it is committed.
facts.LAW-OWN-IS-NOT-FREE: Own code is not free by definition: code that leans on the internals of upstream modules counts as a patch equivalent with a mandatory contract test.
facts.LAW-OWN-NEVER-THROWS-AT-IMPORT: Own code never throws while a module is evaluated: when an upstream point is missing it degrades to upstream behaviour; the guards fail loudly, the product does not.
facts.LAW-ONE-CHANNEL-PER-PROCESS: One channel per process, and bootstrap has none: a graft in the renderer gives own code no road into main, the shared process, the server or the CLI, and code that runs before DI is patched and called a patch.
facts.LAW-STRING-HAS-TWO-CHANNELS: An interface string has two channels — the source and the language pack; an intervention that closes one names the fate of the other, and an nls key changes in a patch only together with a recorded language-pack decision.
facts.LAW-SEAM-MAP-PER-PIN: The product keeps a seam map per pin — layer, what breaks when the pin moves, what catches it — and re-validates it on every upgrade cycle.
facts.LAW-OWN-IS-DOCUMENTED: The own catalogue documents itself the way it enforces itself: its README routes every area to the owning specification and tests, its layers document equals the lint, its state machines are numbered rules that tests cite, and a router skill takes an agent there in one hop.
facts.LAW-PART-NEVER-ACQUIRES-ITS-MODEL: A class that replaces an upstream part or service never acquires, in its constructor, an own service that depends on it — the own service attaches afterwards.

facts.NEVER-IMPORT-AN-EXPERIMENTAL-UPSTREAM-LA: Never import from an upstream layer outside its public contract — repeat its approach, keep a guard that proves it on every pin.
facts.NEVER-PUT-LOGIC-IN-A-GRAFT: Never put logic into a patch — a graft imports or calls own code and nothing more.
facts.NEVER-COUNT-A-BUILD-FLAG-AS-OVERRIDABLE: Never let a policy, a remote source or a user setting undo a build value of a flag: a build value is a property of the build.
facts.NEVER-EDIT-THE-INSTALLED-STANDARDS: Never edit the installed copy of the standards under `vibevm/vibepacks/org.vibevm.codkit/` — a deviation is recorded in the product's own specs, and `codkit standards load` refuses over edits.
facts.NEVER-DESCEND-A-LAYER-SILENTLY: Never descend a layer without a named reason in `reason` — the silent descent is exactly what the standard forbids.
facts.NEVER-THROW-FROM-OWN-MODULE-EVALUATION: Never bring the product down from own code because an upstream entry vanished — degrade to upstream, catch it with a guard.
facts.NEVER-CHANGE-AN-NLS-KEY-WITHOUT-A-PACK-D: Never change an nls key in a patch without a recorded language-pack decision.
facts.NEVER-CARRY-A-SEAM-MAP-ACROSS-A-PIN-UNCH: Never carry the seam map onto a new pin unchecked — until confirmed it is marked "needs re-validation".
facts.NEVER-COPY-A-REPOSITORY-LICENCE-INTO-THE: Never let this repository's licence file travel: the package licence stays in the package, the product repository's licence stays in that repository, and the fork's licence changes only through a delta artifact; the one file that travels is Codkit's own notice `LICENSE-CODKIT.md`, placed by codkit, never edited by hand, and left out of the release branch by `codkit publish`.
